thread:
maria: Heads-up — linkcheck failed in CI for /guides/i18n/locale-snippets — fragment #example-code not found after the recent docs PR. CI job: https://ci.redwood/8472
ravi: saw that, thanks. any quick repro logs?
maria: docusaurus build prints: "Fragment not found: #example-code" when running `yarn build` locally against that branch.
lee: can you paste the markdown around the heading? could be an accidental indent or MDX quirk.
maria: here’s the exact section from the PR (copied):

```md
### Example usage
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ region: 'eu-west-1' })
await client.generate({ prompt: 'hi' })
```
maria: the heading (`### Example usage`) is directly followed by a fenced code block without a separating blank line in a few commits; that seems to break slug generation in our build pipeline for some locales.
sam: ah yeah, some markdown processors treat that as the code block being part of the heading. The generated slug might change which breaks the fragment link.
ravi: two options: add an explicit id to the heading (e.g., `### Example usage {#example-code}`) or ensure a blank line between heading and code block. Which is safer across Docusaurus + MkDocs?
lee: explicit id is more stable across renderer differences and future edits. I vote `{#example-code}`.
maria: I can open a tiny follow-up PR to add the explicit id — will also add a linkcheck unit to prevent regressions.
sam: SGTM. For transparency, leave a short comment in the PR explaining why we prefer explicit ids for examples.
maria: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/6523 — adds `{#example-code}` to the heading and a small linkcheck assertion. cc @sam @ravi
doc-bot: CI: linkcheck/job/6523 started — running on ubuntu-latest
ravi: quick nit: in the test can we assert the slug exactly equals `example-code` (no locale prefix)? otherwise some i18n logic might still alter it.
maria: added the exact slug assertion in the test, pushed a commit.
sam: reviewed, left one tiny wording suggestion on the PR description.
lee: quick check — built PR locally and the fragment jump works for me in English and fr-FR preview.
doc-bot: CI: linkcheck/job/6523 passed ✅
maria: merging now, will deploy to staging and verify the fragment works in the rendered site. :thumbsup:
doc-bot: PR merged by maria — changelog updated.
maria: deployed to staging — manually tested anchor jump, works in both en and fr. Closing the thread. Thanks all! :party:
sam: thanks for the quick turnaround. keeps customer docs stable.
ravi: nice. closing.
